*   Use when high visual quality (smooth shading) is required for point-based surfaces without connectivity [S1].

The claim states that the technique is used when high visual quality (smooth shading) is required for point-based surfaces without connectivity. The evidence explicitly supports this in multiple places: 1) The introduction notes that current systems associate constant normals leading to flat/Gouraud shading, whereas the proposed method provides 'Phong Splats' with 'visual quality which is far superior'. 2) Section 4 states the system targets 'superior visual quality' by combining per-pixel lighting with linear normal fields. 3) The text explicitly mentions that 'we cannot interpolate normal vectors of neighboring splats, since in general no connectivity information is available,' confirming the 'without connectivity' aspect. 4) The generation section describes creating elliptical splats from dense input samples to approximate the surface, fitting a linear normal field to achieve smooth shading.
